submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires retrospectively on the token that completes a compound noun: the head noun of a noun-noun compound such as box in toy box, ticket in train ticket, driver in car driver, pile in sand pile, square in town square, tree in apple tree, car in model car, time in dinner time, loop in pancake loop, or trains in toy trains, or the final subword fragment of a compound word such as he in bookshelf, ber in barber, or keeper in shopkeeper. A lone noun with no compound partner, or the first element of a compound, fires weakly.
